key_insight: Flow-dependent LSQ filter-widths in LES can transmit floating-point perturbations through mesh metrics with little attenuation, so numerical noise may affect the SGS model response.
engineering_relevance: This matters for heterogeneous CPU/GPU simulations because tiny roundoff differences can alter filter-widths and, in sensitive flows, influence predicted transition and turbulence behavior.
method: Analyzed how LSQ filter-width responds to perturbations in mesh metrics for fixed resolved kinematics.
Introduced a scalar max-min compression of directional mesh scales plus bounded velocity-gradient modulation.
Compared the original and modified formulations on heterogeneous architectures to assess perturbation transmission.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on flow past a circular cylinder at Re=3900 and the Taylor-Green vortex at Re=1600, showing near one-to-one disturbance transmission in the cylinder case but no comparable macroscopic effect on orthogonal Taylor-Green grids.
watch_item: The mitigation preserves flow dependence, but its effectiveness may still depend on grid anisotropy and on whether perturbations couple into shear-layer transition.
paper_title: On the transmission of floating-point perturbations in flow-dependent filter-width formulations in Large-Eddy Simulation
